verdicts.note: A first-term commissioner, elected in 2022 by 58 votes [S4], who runs on that record: jail-remodel funding and the East-Lo canal bridges [S1]. A single term keeps it at -1, not -2. Medium is right.

He says every office, the commissioners included, was told to cut operating costs, and 'revenues need to exceed our expenditures – it's math' [S2]. His pamphlet cites 'responsible budgeting' [S1]. That is restraint, pole_a. -1 medium holds. Taxes is correctly omitted: when asked how to grow without new tax burdens he answered only about attracting employers [S2], with no stated position on tax levels. His housing remark (jobs over housing growth) is not on the market-vs-public housing axis and is correctly not scored.

She is the challenger and new to county office, but her case is 16 years on the Othello City Council and 30 years in banking and finance [S1]. That is a proven-record profile, not an outsider one. -1 medium holds.

Tested toward 0, since she also says the county should collect 'the revenue it is legally entitled to' [S3]. That is about collection, not new taxes. 'We can't just keep taxing and taxing our citizenry' [S2], plus a revenue answer built on economic development, existing businesses and grants [S3], is a clear pole_a lean. Without a pledge to cut taxes or oppose a specific levy, -1 rather than -2. Medium holds. Her party preference played no part, correctly.

'Manage budgets, protect taxpayer dollars' [S1] and 'we have to live within our means' with a 'really tight' budget [S2] place her on the restraint side. Both are general framing rather than specific audit or cut proposals, so -1 medium is right.
